book_title: The Book of the Master and the Boy

chapters.title: The Seeker Who Found a Circle
chapters.rationale: The Persian seeker's backstory, his arrival among the quarreling group, the catechetical exchange about praiseworthy speech, and his first public sermon — one continuous movement of arrival and first witness.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Followed
chapters.rationale: From the boy's private approach through the establishment of the relationship — the Master's refusal to spoon-feed, the proof that a guide is needed, and the boy's submission to limits.

chapters.title: The Five Conditions and the Covenant
chapters.rationale: The single Book argument, the five conditions (including secrecy from his father), the long separation, the prostration, and the binding covenant of Hizb Allah — the formal initiation seam.

chapters.title: How Creation Is Made
chapters.rationale: The Master's exposition of will–command–saying, the seven principles, the pairing of zahir and batin, and the imam/hujja/du'at as the inner counterparts of sun/moon/stars — one sustained cosmological teaching.

chapters.title: The World as Parable
chapters.rationale: The defense of the world against ignorant praise and ignorant blame, the parables of heaven, earth, sea, water, and air, culminating in the doctrine of three knowledges (apparent, inner, inner-of-inner) and the question of time.

chapters.title: Outer and Inner, Body and Soul
chapters.rationale: From the boy's plea to be returned to practical sciences through the treatment of ascetics, the unity of zahir and batin, the origin of differing passions, and the justice of God toward differing seekers — one ethical-anthropological arc.

chapters.title: Wealth, Zakat, and the Naming
chapters.rationale: The boy's surrender of property in five shares, the introduction of the higher Shaykh, the boy's renaming as Salih, the seven-day waiting, and the secret instruction at the master's house — one continuous initiation into the inner order.

chapters.title: Returning Home, and the Father's Reckoning
chapters.rationale: The farewell counsel, the parting, the father's angry confrontation, the candid debate, and the father's own conversion — closing the private discipleship arc by extending it to the boy's own household.

chapters.title: Abu Malik and the Trial of the Old Religion
chapters.rationale: The long set-piece in which the established scholar Abu Malik leads his community to investigate, debates Salih on monotheism, justice, prophecy, taqiyya, and the killing of God's guardians, and finally repents — the book's public-doctrinal climax.

chapters.title: The Author's Word
chapters.rationale: The author's own brief note that the narrative form is a confirmation of God's command, followed by the closing blessings — a short codicil best kept distinct from the dramatic ending.
